newsitem.title: USA: Spot U.S. propane falls on warm weather, no demand.
newsitem.headline: Spot U.S. propane falls on warm weather, no demand.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices cratered in midday activity Tuesday that was dominated by sellers concerned about warm weather ahead and further drops in propane, NYMEX futures, players said.
"It's mostly sellers out today. There is little demand," said one Houston trader.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane traded at the open at 59.75 cents before plunging to sales of 56.00 cents.
The midday range was talked between 56.00 cents and 56.50 cents a gallon, 3.50 cents below Monday's levels.
In the Midwest, Conway, Kansas, hub spot material also dropped to a low of 67.00 cents and then crept back up at midday to 70.00/70.25 cents.
"Sellers are concerned about propane being overvalued. With this warm weather, the risk of propane falling is much greater than going back up," said one Conway player.
Weather Services Corp has forecasted above normal temperatures and precipitation in its six to 10 day outlook for the U.S. Northeast.
Warmer weather is also predicted for other U.S. regions.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631
